newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian food firm interim profit up 39 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian food firm interim profit up 39 pct.

text.p: Mauritian food concern Happy World Foods posted a 39 percent rise in interim pre-tax profit to 47.9 million rupees ($2.4 million) for the six months ending 31 December 1996 compared to 34.5 million rupees in the corresponding period in 1995, company officials said on Friday.
But interim profit after tax of Happy World Foods slipped by 2.4 percent to 32.5 million rupees for half-year from 33.3 million rupees during the corresponding period in 1995.
Company officials blamed the lower interim after tax profit for 1996 on provision for a higher tax bill of 15.9 million rupees as compared to 1.2 million rupees in 1995.
Turnover for the last semester of 1996 went up by 28 percent to 548.7 million rupees from 428.4 million rupees during the corresponding period in 1995.

"The taxation charge of 15.9 million rupees comprised an amount of 3.7 million rupees under-provided in the previous financial year, and a substantially higher tax provision of 12.2 million rupees," the company said.
"It should be noted that previous tax losses have all been absorbed and are no longer available to be set off against current tax liabilities," the company added.
In the financial year ending 30 June 1996, Happy World Foods posted a pre-tax profit of 62.2 million rupees, after tax profit of 59.4 million rupees on turnover of 873.9 million rupees.
For the current financial year, Happy World Foods forecasts a turnover of 1.0 billion rupees and pre-tax profit "to grow significantly over the previous year."

"The future developments in the distribution sector may not prove conducive to such strong performance by the company and it appears unlikely that the first semester"s results will be sustained," the company said.
